sections.title: Stage 8 · Prodigy: mental mastery
sections.html:
Stage 8 · Prodigy: mental mastery

Nine lessons, all in the head. Ten 3-digit lines, 3-digit flash, and times and divide on the mental beads. Then money, then numbers below zero. This is expert-level mental arithmetic, and the stage to film.

Where this stage goes

The level goal. Ten 3-digit lines in the head, 3-digit flash, and mental 2 × 2 multiplication. This is expert-level mental arithmetic.

In plain words. Ten three-digit numbers added in the head. Three-digit flash. Two-digit times two-digit mentally. Expert-level mental math. The one to film.

How long. 3–4 months at fifteen minutes a day, six days a week.

Nothing new to learn here. Everything gets bigger and faster. The wooden soroban becomes a warm-up tool, and every drill is mental.

Expect plateaus. They last about two weeks and then break overnight, usually after a day when nothing seemed to happen. Keep the sessions short and daily, and keep the drill the same size through the flat weeks.

Ten mixed 3-digit lines in the head is the format of the Japanese 1st kyu mental exam, the top grade below dan. Your child will meet it in the second lesson.

The drills in this stage

  • Mental. Five, then ten 3-digit lines in the head, plus and minus. Times and divide on the mental beads.
  • Flash. Five, then ten 3-digit numbers, at 1 second and then 0.8 seconds.
  • Life drills. Money sums from real receipts, and sums that drop below zero.

Accuracy before speed

Pass marks drop a little here, to 75 or 80 percent, because the problems are long. The rule does not change. Speed up only after three good sheets in a row. On the ten-line page, under two minutes a problem is the first goal. Exam speed is under forty seconds, and that comes later.

Where this sits on the abacus ladders

Prodigy is the Advanced level in our map to UCMAS. Ten 3-digit lines in the head is the Japanese 1st kyu mental format, and Bead Score rung 15. Five 3-digit numbers flashed at one second is rung 14, around 2nd dan on the flash anzan ladder.

Parent linePlateaus last two weeks and break overnight. Keep the daily drill at the same size.

Lesson 8.1 · Mental: five 3-digit lines, mixed

Lesson 57 of 76. Stage 8, lesson 1 of 9. About 10 minutes. You need no soroban. A pencil for the answers only.

By the end, your child can add and take away five 3-digit lines in the head.

The move

Five lines, three digits, plus and minus. Three rods in the picture, with carries and borrows running between them.

If the picture wobbles, slow the reading down, not the beads. Read one line, move it, then read the next.

Worked example. The first two lines of a head sum.

  • Start with .
  • − 247. Hundreds rod, minus 2: take away 5, add 3. Tens rod, minus 4: add 6, borrow 1 from the left. Hundreds rod, the borrow (minus 1): the beads are there. Ones rod, minus 7: add 3, borrow 1 from the left. Tens rod, the borrow (minus 1): the beads are there. Now .
  • Read it: 368.
Parent lineRead each line aloud for your child the first few days, then let them read it alone.

Drill

No soroban. Read the column, move the beads in your head, write only the answer. Pass mark: 8 of 10 right. Not yet? Same page tomorrow.

Lesson 58 of 76. Stage 8, lesson 2 of 9. About 12 minutes. You need no soroban. A pencil for the answers only.

By the end, your child can add and take away ten 3-digit lines in the head.

The move

The classic exam format. The Japanese 1st kyu mental test is twenty of these in twelve minutes.

Under two minutes a problem is the goal for now. Under forty seconds is exam speed.

Long sums are won by rhythm. Read, move, read, move, at the same beat from the top line to the bottom.

sections.title: Lesson 8.3 · Flash: 3-digit numbers

Lesson 8.3 · Flash: 3-digit numbers

Lesson 59 of 76. Stage 8, lesson 3 of 9. About 8 minutes. You need a grown-up to show or read the numbers. No soroban, no paper.

By the end, your child can add five 3-digit numbers flashed at one second each.

The move

Five 3-digit numbers at one second each. Three rods at once, every number.

At this size the eyes stop reading digits and start taking the number as one shape. That shift is what this page builds.

Worked example. Five 3-digit numbers.

  • Number 1: 265. Mental beads: .
  • Number 2: 783. Mental beads: .
  • Number 3: 142. Mental beads: .
  • Number 4: 684. Mental beads: .
  • Number 5: 340. Mental beads: .
  • Say 2,214.
Parent lineUse big cards and a thick pen, because a number you cannot read at a glance is not a fair flash.

Drill

A grown-up shows each number for 1 second on a card, or says it at that beat, once each. Your child says only the total. Pass mark: 8 of 10 right. Not yet? Same page tomorrow.

Lesson 8.4 · Flash: ten 3-digit numbers

Ten numbers at 0.8 seconds. Breathe. Let each number land.

sections.title: Lesson 8.5 · Mental: 2-digit × 2-digit

Lesson 8.5 · Mental: 2-digit × 2-digit

Lesson 61 of 76. Stage 8, lesson 5 of 9. About 12 minutes. You need no soroban. A pencil for the answers only.

By the end, your child can times a 2-digit number by a 2-digit number in the head.

The move

Four small answers added on the mental beads, left to right, exactly as on the soroban. Each one lands one rod right of the last.

If the picture holds the first two and drops the rest, go back to the soroban for one problem and say the landing rods out loud.

Worked example. 34 × 27 on the mental beads.

  • 3 × 2 = 06. It lands on the thousands and hundreds rods. Beads: .
  • 3 × 7 = 21. It lands on the hundreds and tens rods. Beads: .
  • 4 × 2 = 08. It lands on the hundreds and tens rods. Beads: .
  • 4 × 7 = 28. It lands on the tens and ones rods. Beads: .
  • Read it: 918.
Parent lineMost adults need paper for this one, so let your child try you on it.

Drill

No soroban. Work each small product on the mental beads, left to right. Write only the answer. Pass mark: 8 of 10 right. Not yet? Same page tomorrow.

Lesson 8.6 · Mental: 3-digit × 1-digit

Lesson 62 of 76. Stage 8, lesson 6 of 9. About 10 minutes. You need no soroban. A pencil for the answers only.

By the end, your child can times a 3-digit number by a 1-digit number in the head.

The move

Three small answers on the picture. Hundreds digit first, landing two rods left of the ones place, then tens, then ones.

It is the same problem as Lesson 6.3, with the soroban put away.

Lesson 8.7 · Mental: 3-digit ÷ 1-digit

Lesson 63 of 76. Stage 8, lesson 7 of 9. About 10 minutes. You need no soroban. A pencil for the answers only.

By the end, your child can divide a 3-digit number by a 1-digit number in the head.

The move

Guess, times, take away, on the picture. Hold the number to divide as beads. Watch each part come off as the guesses land.

Say the answer digits as they arrive, then the whole answer at the end.

Worked example. 952 ÷ 7 on the mental beads.

  • Set 952 on the beads: .
  • 7 into 9: 1. Take away 700. Beads: . Answer so far: 1.
  • 7 into 25: 3. Take away 210. Beads: . Answer so far: 13.
  • 7 into 42: 6. Take away 42. Beads: . Answer so far: 136.
  • Read it: 136.
Parent lineIf a guess goes wrong in the head, let your child start over from the top, calmly.

Drill

No soroban. Guess, multiply, take away, on the picture. Write only the answer. Pass mark: 8 of 10 right. Not yet? Same page tomorrow.

sections.title: Lesson 8.8 · Decimals and money
sections.html:
Lesson 8.8 · Decimals and money

Lesson 64 of 76. Stage 8, lesson 8 of 9. About 10 minutes. You need no soroban. A pencil for the answers only.

By the end, your child can add money in the head, dollars and cents, from a list.

The move

Decimals change nothing on the beads. Pick a rod to be the ones, one with a dot on the beam. The rods to its right are tenths and hundredths.

So $12.75 + $3.50 is 1275 + 350 on the beads, with the dot two rods from the right. The beads show 1625. Read it as $16.25.

Then take it shopping. Add the receipt in your head before the till does.

Worked example. $12.75 and $3.50, with the dot two rods from the right.

  • Start with ($12.75).
  • + 350. Hundreds rod, plus 3: add 5, take away 2. Tens rod, plus 5: take away 5, carry 1 to the left. Hundreds rod, the carry (plus 1): the beads are free. Now ($16.25).
  • Read it: $16.25.
Parent lineHand your child the next grocery receipt and a pencil for the total only.

Drill

No soroban. Each line is money. Picture the beads with the dot two rods from the right, and write only the total. Pass mark: 8 of 10 right. Not yet? Same page tomorrow.

sections.title: Lesson 8.9 · Below zero
sections.html:
Lesson 8.9 · Below zero

Lesson 65 of 76. Stage 8, lesson 9 of 9. About 10 minutes. You need no soroban. A pencil for the answers only.

By the end, your child can work a sum that drops below zero and say the answer with its minus sign.

The move

A soroban cannot show a number below zero. So soroban users borrow from an empty rod on the far left.

Take 20 − 35. It will not fit. Borrow 100: now it is 120 − 35 = 85. The beads show 85. But you borrowed 100, so give it back. 100 − 85 = 15, and the answer is below zero: minus 15.

Try a few on paper first, then in the head. This is rare in exams and useful in life, from temperatures to bank balances.

Worked example. 20 − 35, with a borrowed 100.

  • 20 − 35 will not fit. Borrow 100 from an empty rod on the left. Now it is 120 − 35.
  • Work it on the beads: .
  • You borrowed 100, so give it back: 100 − 85 = 15, and it is below zero.
  • Read it: −15.
Parent lineUse a thermometer or a game score to show why numbers below zero are real.

Drill

No soroban. Borrow 100 from an empty rod when a line will not fit, then give it back at the end. Write the answer with its minus sign. Pass mark: 8 of 10 right. Not yet? Same page tomorrow.

sections.title: The Prodigy Boss
sections.html:
The Prodigy Boss

This is the boss to film. Take it when every lesson is passed and the ten-line page holds 8 of 10. Part 1 maps to Lesson 8.2. Part 2 maps to 8.3. Part 3 maps to 8.5. Part 4 maps to 8.7.

The printed test is Boss 8 in boss-tests.md. It has 4 parts:

  • Ten 3-digit lines. 4 problems, 6 minutes. Need 3 of 4 in 6 minutes.
  • Flash 3-digit. 5 rounds, five numbers at 1 s. Need 4 of 5 in 3 minutes 20 seconds.
  • Mental 2 × 2. 5 problems. Need 4 of 5 in 4 minutes.
  • Mental ÷. 5 problems, 3-digit ÷ 1-digit. Need 4 of 5 in 2 minutes 30 seconds.

sections.title: What the trainer adds to this stage
sections.html:
What the trainer adds to this stage

From here, the trainer does the jobs a parent cannot. It flashes 3-digit numbers at exact speeds. It times ten-line sums to the second. And it plots each Bead Score on the age chart.

The paper pages here are a full set of mental drills you can run anywhere: the car, a waiting room, a trip. The trainer is the stopwatch and the flash cards.
